newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul clarifies request to pension funds on stocks.
newsitem.headline: Seoul clarifies request to pension funds on stocks.

text.p: South Korean authorities are encouraging -- not ordering -- public pension funds to buy stocks, a finance ministry official said on Thursday.

The official, who declined to be named, said a finance ministry request to three public pension funds on Wednesday to buy into the depressed market was a way of helping the fund managers overcome internal objections and increase their stock portfolio holdings.
"It's like Koreans, they won't sing unless you ask them to," he said.
"The pension funds want to invest in the stock market, but there are a number of internal guidelines that made it difficult for them," he said. "We're just making it easier for them."
Finance ministry officials had asked the heads of three large pension funds to buy a combined 300 billion won worth of shares by the end of the year.

The news sent prices of blue-chip shares soaring on Thursday on expectations that the funds would comply with the request. However, by late Thursday there was no evidence the funds had started buying.

The official said the National Pension Fund was asked to purchase 150 billion won worth of shares, the Government Employees' Pension Fund 100 billion won, and the Korea Teachers' Pension Fund 50 billion won.
But he denied the government was pressuring the funds.
"If they don't want to buy stocks, they'll say no and that's the end of the story," he said. "We suggested that those amounts would be appropriate for them to purchase."
He added: "If you want to think we intervened in the market, then we did. If you don't want to think we intervened, we didn't."
The stock investments would be made through purchases of beneficiary certificates from investment trust companies, the official said.

The three pension funds hold an average of 5.9 percent of their total investments in the stock market, far lower than the equity holdings of their counterparts in developed nations, the official said.
Average stock holdings of all public funds, including pension funds, was only about 1.6 percent.
